name_note: GTDB g__Bacteroides is narrower than the classical genus: part of the NCBI Bacteroides genomes, including the vulgatus and dorei group, are placed in Phocaeicola instead.

sentences.text: Bacteroides are anaerobic, non-spore-forming Gram-negative bacteria that are resistant to bile acids and are major members of the human gastrointestinal tract.
They metabolise dietary polysaccharides and oligosaccharides, supplying nutrition and vitamins to the host and to other microbes living in the intestine.
The genome of Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, a dominant gut member, encodes an extensive apparatus for taking up and breaking down polysaccharides the host cannot digest.
A century of study of this readily cultured, genetically tractable group has given insight into the biochemistry, genomics and ecology of gut bacteria.

Although usually commensal, some species have been reported as opportunistic pathogens in GI disease, trauma, cancer or surgery, and studies have associated lower gut Bacteroides levels with inflammatory bowel disease.
